11.1: Arjuna: out of compassion you have spoken the supreme secret of the Self, and my delusion is gone.
11.2: I have heard in detail of the origin and dissolution of beings, and of your imperishable greatness.
11.3: As you have described yourself, so it is — yet I wish to see your divine form.
11.4: If you think I can bear the sight, show me your imperishable Self.
11.5: Krishna consents: behold My hundreds and thousands of divine forms, of many colours and shapes.
11.6: Behold the Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, Ashvins and Maruts — many marvels never seen before.
11.7: See here the whole universe, moving and unmoving, standing together in My body — and whatever else you wish to see.
11.8: But you cannot see Me with these eyes; I give you a divine eye — behold My sovereign power.
11.9: Sanjaya narrates: having spoken thus, the great Lord of yoga showed His supreme form.
11.10: A form of many mouths and eyes, many wondrous sights, many divine ornaments and uplifted weapons.
11.11: Wearing divine garlands and robes, anointed with divine fragrance, all-wonderful, infinite, facing every direction.
11.12: If a thousand suns rose together in the sky, that splendour might resemble the radiance of that mighty Self.
11.13: There Arjuna saw the whole universe, divided in many ways, gathered together in the body of the God of gods.
11.14: Overcome with wonder, hair standing on end, Arjuna bowed his head and spoke with joined palms.
11.15: I see all the gods in your body, and all beings, Brahma on his lotus seat, the sages and celestial serpents.
11.16: I see you with countless arms, bellies, mouths and eyes, infinite on every side — with no beginning, middle or end.
11.17: I see you with crown, mace and disc, a mass of radiance shining everywhere, hard to look upon, immeasurable.
11.18: You are the imperishable, the supreme to be known, the ultimate support, the guardian of eternal dharma.
11.19: Without beginning, middle or end, of infinite power and countless arms, the sun and moon your eyes, your mouth a blazing fire.
11.20: You alone fill the space between earth and heaven and all the quarters; seeing this fearful form, the three worlds tremble.
11.21: Hosts of gods enter you; some in fear praise you with joined palms; the great sages hail you with hymns.
11.22: The Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, Vishvadevas, Ashvins, Maruts, ancestors and hosts of celestials gaze on you in wonder.
11.23: Seeing your immense form with many mouths, eyes, arms, thighs, feet and terrible tusks, the worlds are shaken — and so am I.
11.24: Seeing you touching the sky, blazing in many colours, mouths open and eyes shining, my inmost self trembles and I find no peace.
11.25: Seeing your mouths with terrible tusks like the fires of destruction, I lose my bearings — be gracious, Lord of the worlds.
11.26: All the sons of Dhritarashtra, with the host of kings, Bhishma, Drona and Karna, along with our warriors too —
11.27: — rush into your fearful mouths with terrible tusks; some are seen crushed between your teeth, heads pulverised.
11.28: As rivers rush towards the ocean, so these heroes of the world enter your blazing mouths.
11.29: As moths rush into a flame to their destruction, so these creatures rush into your mouths to perish.
11.30: You lick up and devour all the worlds with your flaming mouths; your fierce rays scorch the whole universe.
11.31: Tell me who you are in this terrible form; I bow to you — I wish to know you, the primal one, for I do not understand your working.
11.32: The most quoted line: I am Time, the mighty destroyer of worlds, come to annihilate these people; even without you they will not survive.
11.33: Therefore stand up and win glory; conquer your enemies and enjoy a prosperous kingdom — they are already slain by Me; be only the instrument.
11.34: Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna and the other warriors are killed by Me — do not be distressed; fight and you will conquer.
11.35: Sanjaya: hearing this, trembling and with joined palms, Arjuna bowed again and spoke to Krishna in a faltering voice.
11.36: Arjuna: rightly does the world rejoice in your praise; demons flee and the perfected bow to you.
11.37: Why should they not bow to you, greater than Brahma, the primal cause, infinite, Lord of gods, refuge of the universe?
11.38: You are the primal God, the ancient Person, the supreme resting place, knower and known, the highest abode; the universe is pervaded by you.
11.39: You are Vayu, Yama, Agni, Varuna, the moon, the Lord of creatures and the great-grandsire — salutations a thousand times over.
11.40: Salutations to you before and behind and on every side; of infinite power and immeasurable strength, you pervade all and are all.
11.41: Arjuna's apology: whatever I said rashly out of carelessness or love, calling you friend, Krishna, comrade, not knowing your greatness —
11.42: — and if I disrespected you in jest, while resting, sitting or eating, alone or before others, forgive me, immeasurable one.
11.43: You are the father of this world, the guru worthy of worship; there is none equal to you — how could there be one greater?
11.44: Therefore I bow and prostrate and beg your grace; bear with me as a father with a son, a friend with a friend, a lover with the beloved.
11.45: I am delighted to have seen what was never seen before, and yet my mind is troubled with fear — show me the form I know.
11.46: I wish to see you as before, with crown, mace and disc — assume that four-armed form, thousand-armed one.
11.47: Krishna: by My grace and My power you have been shown this supreme, radiant, universal, infinite, primal form that no one else has seen.
11.48: Not by Vedas or sacrifice or study or charity or rites or severe austerities can I be seen in this form in the world of men.
11.49: Do not be afraid or bewildered at seeing this terrible form; free from fear and glad at heart, behold My other form again.
11.50: Sanjaya: having spoken thus, Krishna showed His own form again, and the great one consoled the terrified Arjuna by becoming gentle.
11.51: Arjuna: seeing your gentle human form again, my mind is composed and I have returned to my own nature.
11.52: Krishna: this form of Mine is very hard to see; even the gods long constantly for a glimpse of it.
11.53: Not by the Vedas, austerity, charity or sacrifice can I be seen as you have seen Me.
11.54: But by single-minded devotion alone can I be known, seen in truth and entered into.
11.55: The closing instruction: one who works for Me, holds Me supreme, is devoted to Me, free of attachment and without enmity to any being — comes to Me.
